problem_statement:
Title: Missing process capability interface and privilege checks

In a build configured with CONFIG_SCHED_CAPABILITIES, an application that includes <sys/prctl.h> and uses PR_CAPS_GET, PR_CAPS_DROP, PR_CAP_RAWIO, PR_CAP_SPAWN, PR_CAP_ADMIN, or PR_CAP_ALL fails to compile because the kernel does not provide these definitions.

Even if those definitions were present, the expected runtime behavior is missing: a process has no way to reduce its privileges, and dropping a capability does not cause the guarded operation to fail. In particular, after a process calls prctl(PR_CAPS_DROP, PR_CAP_SPAWN), it can still successfully call task_create(); after a process calls prctl(PR_CAPS_DROP, PR_CAP_RAWIO), it can still successfully call mount() when a mountable filesystem is available. If the system has no mountable filesystem, mount() may fail with ENOSYS because no filesystem is available; when a mountable filesystem is available, dropping PR_CAP_RAWIO must cause mount() to fail with EPERM.

The kernel should provide a process capability mechanism controlled by CONFIG_SCHED_CAPABILITIES. When the option is disabled, the existing behavior should remain, and prctl() should reject PR_CAPS_GET and PR_CAPS_DROP. When the option is enabled, every process should start with all capabilities, kernel threads should hold all capabilities, and a child task should inherit the capability set of its creator at the time of creation.

The required interface behavior is:

- prctl(PR_CAPS_GET) returns the current capability set of the calling process.
- prctl(PR_CAPS_DROP, mask) removes the named capabilities from the calling process and only removes capabilities; it does not grant or restore capabilities. Once dropped, a capability cannot be gained again by that process.
- A child task created after a drop sees the reduced set, while a child created before the drop retains the capabilities it inherited.
- PR_CAP_RAWIO, PR_CAP_SPAWN, PR_CAP_ADMIN, and PR_CAP_ALL must be defined, with PR_CAP_ALL meaning all capabilities.

The required enforcement behavior is:

- If PR_CAP_SPAWN has been dropped, task_create() must fail with EPERM.
- If PR_CAP_RAWIO has been dropped, mounting a filesystem must fail with EPERM when a mountable filesystem is available; if no mountable filesystem is available, mount() may fail with ENOSYS instead.
- PR_CAP_ADMIN must guard administrative board-control operations, so a process without PR_CAP_ADMIN must not be able to request administrative board actions.

The restrictions should apply to user-space calls in flat and protected builds, and an operation performed on behalf of a process should be subject to that process's capability set. A process that drops all three capabilities should subsequently be unable to create a task, mount a filesystem, or perform administrative board-control requests, while prctl(PR_CAPS_GET) should report that no capabilities remain. A process that has not dropped a capability must remain unaffected.

superseded_statements.problem_statement: The ostest caps test requires a process-capability subsystem: a task's capability set readable and droppable via prctl(PR_CAPS_GET/PR_CAPS_DROP), with PR_CAP_RAWIO/PR_CAP_SPAWN/PR_CAP_ADMIN inherited from the creator's group, and the SPAWN and RAWIO checks enforced by task_create()/mount() returning EPERM once the relevant capability is dropped. With the old kernel this subsystem (CONFIG_SCHED_CAPABILITIES and the prctl PR_CAPS_* options and PR_CAP_* bit definitions) does not exist, so the test compiles to nothing and never runs; the behavior it asserts (child full set, grandchild reduced set, EPERM on task_create and mount after dropping SPAWN/RAWIO, empty set after dropping all) must be present for the test to pass.

Describe only the observable symptom, its trigger and the required behavior, not what the code checks or must do internally

superseded_statements.problem_statement:
An apps change adds a new capabilities test to testing/ostest. When CONFIG_SCHED_CAPABILITIES=y and CONFIG_SCHED_WAITPID=y in a flat or protected build, i.e. when CONFIG_BUILD_KERNEL is not set, the ostest build includes testing/ostest/caps.c. In the current kernel the build fails because caps.c uses PR_CAPS_DROP, PR_CAPS_GET, PR_CAP_ALL, PR_CAP_SPAWN, PR_CAP_RAWIO, and PR_CAP_ADMIN, and those identifiers are undeclared.

The expected result is that, with the capability feature enabled, ostest builds and caps_test runs and reports PASSED. The test observes that a child process starts with the full capability set, can query its current set, and can request removal of capabilities; after the capability used by task spawning is removed, task_create() fails with EPERM; after the capability used by raw I/O is removed, mount() fails with EPERM, or ENOSYS if no mountable filesystem is configured; a child created after the reduced set is observed to see the reduced set; and a parent that has not dropped the capability retains the full set. When CONFIG_SCHED_CAPABILITIES is not set, the caps test is not built and ostest behavior is unchanged.
